Question B-003-020-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Open-wire line can carry high RF voltage, so contact during transmission can burn the person touching it.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Because high-voltage radio energy might burn the person": This is the correct choice because open-wire line can carry high RF voltage, so contact during transmission can burn the person touching it.
- sourceIndex 1: "Because contact might break the transmission line": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Because high-voltage radio energy might burn the person. In lightning protection, tower work, antenna contact hazards, and safe antenna servicing, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 2: "Because contact might cause spurious emissions": This answer would fit a different fault than Because high-voltage radio energy might burn the person. In lightning protection, tower work, antenna contact hazards, and safe antenna servicing, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Because contact might cause a short circuit and damage the transmitter": This option confuses another station topic with Because high-voltage radio energy might burn the person. In lightning protection, tower work, antenna contact hazards, and safe antenna servicing, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
